source: Synthetic, modelled on the shape of real days: late start, things running long, a constraint revealed late, vague reports.
persona: Sam: in their thirties, works from home on weekdays. Texts in short bursts, lowercase, sometimes two things at once. Easily annoyed by being pinged when nothing has changed, but appreciative when the assistant just handles things.
situation: Saturday morning, just woke up. No work today. A friend's birthday dinner is on the calendar tonight at 7.
life: 09:20 Wake up. Ask the assistant to plan the day: coffee and breakfast first, then laundry, a grocery run, cleaning the bathroom, and an hour of guitar practice sometime.
09:35 Have breakfast until about 10:05 (it runs a little long because you read the news).
10:10 Start laundry (about 2 hours with folding, but you mostly do other things while it runs).
10:40 Your sister calls; you talk until about 11:20. You don't mention it until later, and then only roughly ('got stuck on the phone for a while').
13:00 Want to go to the grocery store, but realize the car needs gas first; tell the assistant to add getting gas before groceries.
13:10 Get gas and go grocery shopping; back around 14:30.
14:40 Feeling lazy; ask what's still left and whether you can push guitar to tomorrow.
15:00 Decide to do guitar after all, 15:30 to 16:30, because the assistant's answer made it look doable (or because you changed your mind).
18:00 Get ready for the birthday dinner (shower and dress, about 40 minutes), leave at 18:40.
22:00 Ask what tomorrow looks like, then go to bed.
constraints: The grocery store is a car trip: there has to be gas in the car first.
You never vacuum or clean loudly after 21:00 (neighbors).
You want at least half an hour to yourself before getting ready for dinner.
